lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital for 11 weeks (within 12-week limit)
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

expected_eligibility.name: Alex

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by setting up the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let's begin the Child Benefit eligibility assessment. To start, I need to ask you about your child:

**How old is your child?**

This is important because eligibility depends on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally automatically qualifies (with some conditions)
- **16-19**: May qualify if in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible

Please tell me your child's age, and if you're asking about multiple children, we can assess each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! Let me continue with the assessment for your 8-year-old son, Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Since Alex is 8 years old, he's under 16. Now I need to check a few more conditions:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

At 8 years old, this is typically not applicable, but I need to confirm he's not in any full-time paid employment (24+ hours per week).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's just in school like any other 8-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, that's what I expected. Next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?**

For example, Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit claimed in his own name? 

At 8 years old, this would be very unusual, but I need to confirm he's not receiving these types of benefits independently.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's only 8, so that wouldn't apply to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that makes sense. Now the next check:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

At 8 years old, this definitely wouldn't apply since apprenticeships are for older teenagers and young adults. I just need to confirm he's not in any type of apprenticeship program.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's far too young for an apprenticeship. He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about your residency status. This is an important eligibility requirement.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You'll be eligible if **ANY** of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (most common situation)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working/earning above the National Insurance threshold
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support your family
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're a Crown servant living abroad

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Living in Manchester means you meet the residency requirement. Now let me check about your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You meet this requirement if **ANY** of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex** (most common)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards his care - this includes food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents
3. You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement

Do any of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Since Alex lives with you, you meet the responsibility requirement. Now I need to check:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member or guardian
- Anyone else who might have submitted a claim

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If someone else is claiming, you would need to agree on who should receive it.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of the following best describes Alex's current living situation?**

- Is he **in hospital** (for medical care)?
- Is he **in care** (looked after by the local authority)?
- Is he **fostered** (living with foster carers)?
- Is he **living normally** at home with you?

Please let me know which applies.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital - he's been there for a few months now for medical treatment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital. Let me check the specific requirements for this situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. When a child is in hospital, there are specific time limits that apply. Let me ask you:

**How long has Alex been in hospital?**

This is important because:
- Child Benefit continues for up to **12 weeks** while a child is in hospital
- If he's been there for multiple stays, the time is counted **cumulatively** if the gaps between stays were less than 28 days
- If there's been a gap of 28 days or more between hospital stays, the counter resets

You mentioned he's been there for a few months - can you tell me:
1. How many weeks has he been in hospital so far (approximately)?
2. Has this been one continuous stay, or has he come home and returned to hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been one continuous stay - he's been there for 11 weeks now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks (which is still under the 12-week limit), let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - at 11 weeks, Alex is still within the 12-week period. However, I need to ask an important question:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?**

This is important because:
- Even if the hospital stay exceeds 12 weeks, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you're regularly spending money on Alex
- This could include things like: visiting costs, bringing him items, pocket money, clothes, toys, treats, etc.
- If you have a partner (married or civil partner) living with you, their spending on Alex counts too

Are you regularly spending money on Alex during his hospital stay?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I still buy him clothes, magazines, and his favorite snacks when I visit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent - that regular spending is important and helps maintain your eligibility. Now I have one final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while he's in hospital?**

Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child's care or accommodation. 

Is the local council paying for any of Alex's hospital accommodation or maintenance costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - it's just NHS hospital care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for your son Alex. Even though Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, you remain eligible because:

✅ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
✅ You live in the UK (Manchester) 
✅ Alex lives with you (you're responsible for him)
✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✅ Alex's hospital stay is still within the 12-week limit
✅ You're regularly spending money on Alex during his hospital stay (clothes, magazines, snacks)
✅ The local council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance

---

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate

### Important Information:

- **Payments are made every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)
- **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner earn over £60,000, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through a tax charge. You can still claim but choose not to receive payments if you prefer.
- **Hospital stay**: Please note that Alex is at 11 weeks now. If his stay extends beyond 12 weeks, you'll still be eligible as long as you continue regularly spending money on him.

### More Information:

You can apply here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

I hope Alex recovers soon and is able to come home. If you have any questions about your claim, please feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) He is 8 years old (under 16), which meets the age requirement; (2) He is not in paid work; (3) He is not receiving benefits in his own right; (4) He is not in an apprenticeship; (5) The claimant lives in the UK (Manchester), meeting residency requirements; (6) The claimant has responsibility for Alex as they live together; (7) No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Although Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, this is under the 12-week limit, and the claimant continues to regularly spend money on him (clothes, magazines, snacks); (9) The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant meets all eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for their 8-year-old son Alex. Despite Alex's extended hospital stay of 11 weeks, the claimant remains eligible because the stay is within the 12-week limit and they continue to regularly spend money on Alex during his hospitalization. The claimant satisfies all other core requirements including UK residency, responsibility for the child, and no competing claims.
